posts.title: Coastal Light: A Morning in the Fog
posts.excerpt: Quiet frames from a foggy morning along the coast.
posts.content:
The fog rolled in just before sunrise. For forty minutes the world was a soft grey wash — the perfect canvas.

The setting

A small cove, three stones and a line of gulls. Everything else was soft focus.

The story

These are not portraits of the coast — they are portraits of the light, the patience and the quiet.

posts.title: Portraits in Soft Window Light
posts.excerpt: Natural light, simple backgrounds, honest expressions.
posts.content:
The best portraits happen when the subject forgets the camera exists. We shoot near large windows at mid-morning.

Light

Large, soft, directional — it flatters skin without washing out detail.

Expression

We ask about hobbies and memories. The result is an image that feels like a conversation, not a pose.

posts.title: Street Photography: City After Rain
posts.excerpt: Reflections and wet streets after a summer storm.
posts.content:
An hour after the storm, the city turned into a mirror. Every puddle held the sky.

The lens

A fast prime, a shallow depth of field and a willingness to wait.

The images in this series are about contrast — the sharp edge of a building against the soft blur of a wet street.
